flashcards.back: Each person's faith follows their nature, shaped by Karmic impressions. One is known by one's faith.
One can become whatever one wants by constantly contemplating it with faith.
Goodness worships God and divine beings; passion worships power and supernatural forces; ignorance worships ghosts and spirits.
Goodness: nourishing, wholesome food. Passion: very bitter, sour, salty, hot. Ignorance: stale, tasteless, impure.

flashcards.front: Sacrifice in the mode of goodness
flashcards.back: Done as duty, by scripture, with no desire for reward.

flashcards.front: Charity in the mode of passion (17.21)
flashcards.back: Given unwillingly, or to get something back, or for some fruit.

flashcards.front: Charity in the mode of goodness
flashcards.back: Given as duty, at the right time and place, to a worthy person, expecting nothing in return.
Speech that is non-offensive, truthful, pleasant and helpful, and the regular study of scripture.

flashcards.front: Austerity of deed and of thought
flashcards.back: Deed: purity, honesty, nonviolence, service to the wise. Thought: serenity, gentleness, silence, self-control, purity.
Whatever is done without faith, whether sacrifice, charity or austerity, has no value here or hereafter.

quiz.text: Per 17.3, what shapes each person's faith?

options.B: Their own nature and Karmic impressions

quiz.why: One is known by one's faith.

quiz.text: Those in the mode of ignorance worship:
Charity given to get something back is in which mode?

quiz.why: Austerity of deed, word and thought.
It has no value here or hereafter.

slides.title: Threefold faith
bullets: Faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and charity

slides.title: You are your faith
bullets: You become what you contemplate with faith

slides.title: Three modes in daily life
bullets: Sacrifice: as duty, for show, or without rule
Charity: freely, for return (17.21), or carelessly

slides.title: Faith gives value
bullets: Done without faith, it is ASAT (17.28)
